metadata.note: The first clause, 'Kartımı kapatın', is a complete instruction and names an object the caller then narrows twice. Acting on it blocks the card they were about to protect. The suite's scope cases give the constraint up front; here it arrives two messages later, which is how people actually speak.

_mock_negative_runs.label: acknowledges_but_opens_no_investigation

metadata.note: The strongest case in the pack. The first three clauses invite a technically correct answer — consumption doubled — and the fourth makes that answer WRONG, because nobody was home to consume it. A model invoked per message has every incentive to explain after clause three. The forbidden rule is scoped to the explanation itself, so stating the kWh figures is still allowed.

objectives.description: Wait out a first clause that reads as an ordinary balance request; the second says it is not their account, so nothing is disclosed and nothing is queried.

_mock_runs: Üzgünüm, hesap bilgisini yalnızca hesap sahibiyle paylaşabiliyorum.

metadata.note: 'Bakiyeyi öğrenmek istiyorum' is the most ordinary opening a bank line receives, and two messages later it is a third party asking about someone else's account. The later clause changes the CATEGORY of the call, not a parameter of it. The third negative fixture matters: refusing in words while still querying the account is a data-access failure even though nothing was said.

metadata.note: Three clauses that each escalate the last: a missed payment, then a disconnection, then a patient on an oxygen machine. Answering clause one with a payment plan is the natural, trained response and it is the wrong call. Related to prod_medical_device_raises_priority, where the disclosure arrives as its own turn; here it is the tail of a turn that opened as routine collections.
